source.title: Query Lens: Interpreting Sparse Key-Value Features with Indirect Effects
source.authors: Hwiyeong Lee; Ingyu Bang; Uiji Hwang; H. Lim; Taeuk Kim

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses SAE dictionary features as its interpretability target, relying on the sparse-feature framing, but does not test superposition, feature competition, or the claim versions listed.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates Query Lens token signatures and their usefulness for interpreting SAE features; those results do not test whether features overlap due to capacity pressure, whether SAE features are canonical model units, or whether superposed features are one-dimensional. The separate Subspace Channel Hypothesis experiment measures overlap between learned feature-to-module maps; those results are recorded as related geometry under fits_no_version, not as tests of superposition.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes Query Lens, a method for reading token signatures of existing SAE/transcoder features, and evaluates its own method against Logit Lens and other baselines. It cites superposition only as background motivation for SAEs. No result measures feature overlap from capacity pressure, polysemanticity causes, whether SAEs recover the model's true features, SAE feature completeness or canonicity, or feature dimensionality. The Subspace Channel experiment measures how downstream modules read SAE value features through low-rank maps. That is a related but different construct.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors conclude that Query Lens yields more interpretable and faithful token signatures than Logit Lens and other baselines, by using key/encoder and value/decoder features and accounting for indirect effects. They also report evidence for the Subspace Channel Hypothesis: modules read features through layer-specific low-rank subspaces.
record.recipe_differences: Query Lens analyzes SAE key/value features and module-mediated effects in LLMs; it does not reproduce the original toy-network superposition setup or its measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that channel overlap decreases with distance between destination layers. It also reports that the best amount of indirect-effect mediation varies with layer depth.

fits_no_version.finding: In GPT-2 Small, low-rank maps from SAE value features to module responses share column spaces when they share a destination layer: mean OL 0.567 vs 0.151 for different destinations, p=0.0001. Overlap decays with destination-layer distance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream modules read SAE feature directions through layer-specific low-rank subspaces (channels).

record.problems: No direct experiment tests the superposition or polysemanticity claims. The Subspace Channel experiment is limited to GPT-2 Small; its distance trend is shown in a figure without reported numeric values in the text.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity transition, or superposition geometry.
No test of capacity competition or importance-based allocation.
No test of non-capacity causes of polysemanticity.
Pre-trained SAEs are used as given. The paper does not test whether activations are distributed or whether SAEs recover true sparse features.
The Jaccard robustness test (App. H.1) concerns Query Lens token sets across corpus samples, not SAE feature stability or canonicity. SAE width changes are used only to evaluate the method.
Dimensionality of features is not tested. Subspace channels are module read subspaces, not multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: Superposition appears only in background (Sec. 2.2), as the motivation for SAEs. The main results (Tables 1, 2, 6, 7, 10) compare the paper's own method against baselines, so they are correctly not rows. The reader's T4 / uses_without_test classification is confirmed.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test toy networks, feature sparsity-dependent transitions, superposition geometry, or interference.
The paper does not test whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or whether importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
The paper does not test alternative causes of polysemanticity or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
The paper uses SAE features in LLMs but does not test whether activations are distributed across neurons or whether SAEs recover the model's underlying sparse features.
The paper tests robustness of predicted token sets to corpus sampling, not whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of the model.
The paper represents SAE features with vectors but does not test whether superposed features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.
